column8: Thu 19 Nov: 3b and 2.2, one clause: known needs bought ahead, unknown needs kept back maps the IPS's two halves (l.11-12, l.15-16) onto the textbook's motives for corporate cash; the mapping is half inverted (a firm keeps cash for the unknown, Laura keeps shares), so it never stands without row 2's limit; pedigree-plus, not an aha.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b and 3e: the hedging motive (keep most when needs come in lean years) is the strongest relation of idea 1 and sits on IPS l.9; Q39-012 already holds its ancestor (Froot, Scharfstein and Stein), so one of the two carries it; followed through it argues for the flexibility in Treasuries, which is the 3e limit; read Acharya, Almeida and Campello before citing them.

Thu 19 Nov: the break of row 1 is NUM-011's finding; the third smaller is NUMBERS 8f (median about $15,200 against $23,000), not 8o as the card cites; say too that the excess is Treasury money, so her flexibility plus anything above the top keeps a median about $23,300 in falls (8f).

Thu 19 Nov: the same market-value-of-spare-cash studies as Q154-030 (Faulkender and Wang), adding Pinkowitz and Williamson via Damodaran; originals unread; co-sponsors not counting unpromised money is already 3d's settled count, so store only.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a pedigree, one clause: a Treasury bought at market is zero NPV, so certainty costs expected return, not value; keep apart from SKELETON 3a's deposit-not-fee line, which is about the extra Treasuries coming back to her (about $46,600 if rates hold), a different reason.

Thu 19 Nov: the $200 million to $90 million illustration is H6-006's principle (a cash flow takes the rate of its own risk; costing the ten at a share return is the error); keep the illustration as H6-006's example, store only.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 or 3f, the aha of the card: zero NPV holds for a diversified owner and stops at Laura, whose career already moves with shares (IPS l.9), so the Treasuries are worth more to her than their price; say worth more to her than to the market, never positive NPV (NPV is the market's measure); competes with H9-010 and Q1-012 for 2.3's clause.

Thu 19 Nov: NUMBERS 8n's option table (A $186,000 and $159,000, E $201,000 and $134,000, checked) read as row 5's trade; Q33-031 already carries the table with the plan's row; never present option A or E as Laura's plan.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f and 3d, middle-strength aha (a missed January as truncation, not a $50,000 shortfall); fix: never a missed 2036 payment as the first plan's risk, since its danger was one date, 1 Jan 2033 (NUMBERS 8s), so say a short reserve that day leaves the residency's last years unfunded; the ladder protects the chain from lack of money only (card Q77).
Thu 19 Nov: 3d, half a clause beside SD-3 (Q150-019): doubt about the money makes distress real, and an owned figure removes the doubt; the 10-25% is firms' studies, never a residency figure.
Thu 19 Nov: survival compounding is H6-010's joint test over ten payments; textbook; the first plan's risk sat on one date (NUMBERS 8s), as the card itself notes.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a, one clause: the textbook calls one rate per cash-flow year not worth the effort because a valuer's error is a small percentage; a payer's error is a short cheque on a date, so the ten take the purist route; extends H7-005 (dedication) with the waiver's reason; pedigree-plus.
Thu 19 Nov: banks match average duration because matching each cash flow is hard; same relation as row 12 and H7-005, carried by row 12.
Thu 19 Nov: the forgotten reinvestment test is H6-004 and H7-001; H6-004's use already prices the gap at zero interest (the extra Treasuries), so the cost of honouring it is not new.
Thu 19 Nov: store; supports row 12: valuers bother with year-by-year rates only in crises or steep curves (6 Nov 2026: 1-year 4.33%, 10-year 4.86%, checked), while a payer bothers always.
Thu 19 Nov: currency, not domicile, is H7-089 (match the currency; Disney's Rio park in dollars); nothing new for the plan.
Thu 19 Nov: store, input to row 18: Taiwan's curve on 18 Nov (2-year 1.51%, 5-year 1.78%, 10-year 1.88%) via search extracts; the CBC auction is the primary source to cite.

Thu 19 Nov: 3e limit and Table 3 row 7, an aha: the US-Taiwan rate gap prices the Taiwan dollar for 2033 near its 25-year strongest (27.52); fixes: one date and the register's spot (32.768 on 6 Nov, NUMBERS 8d), which puts the forward about 27.6; take the need from 8d ($21,930 at 27.52), not a new figure; a hedge's price, never a forecast; Laura cannot buy one (derivatives are banned).

Thu 19 Nov: the $21,500 need is NUMBERS 8d's 27.52 case ($21,930 on the top), already Q10-025's adapted note; labels checked (her flexibility $21,179; her flexibility plus anything above the top $28,682, WORDS l.28); row 18 carries the new point.

Thu 19 Nov: store; Damodaran's test is about expected inflation, and Taiwan's October CPI set against a US long-run assumption is not it; the gap can persist (row 21), so never say Taiwan's rates must rise; one year of rising yields is a fact, not a trend.
Thu 19 Nov: the break that keeps row 18 honest (a forward is a price, not a forecast); Fama (1984) unread, so read it or a survey before use; the NT$-weaker-than-2000 half is Q10-018.
Thu 19 Nov: Table 3 row 7, a second watch figure at most; it rests on row 20's claim that the gap must close, which does not hold, so drop the harmless-way line; a watch changes no rule (IPS l.17).
Thu 19 Nov: store only; Taiwan's country risk figures and a Taiwan-dollar riskless rate serve no decision (no Taiwan-dollar holdings); never a default spread as the residency's Taiwan risk.

Thu 19 Nov: store; blog extract: country risk follows operations, so the money held outside Taiwan does not remove the residency's own risk; at most a 3e clause, never that the plan escapes Taiwan risk.
Thu 19 Nov: 3e structure only (tree for dated steps, scenario for a Taiwan shock, simulation for shares); a method, changes no decision.

Thu 19 Nov: 3f pedigree: Damodaran's simulation with constraints names how the 27 Sep check priced the ladder (about 1 in 31 against none, NUMBERS 8s); a label for an existing finding, never 3.2% fails high.
Thu 19 Nov: store; why no stated figure rests on a simulation (both ends owned); sits beside H7-034 and aha row 1, adds only a quote.
Thu 19 Nov: store, pedigree for H3-014: the plan holds no rate view (buys on the January 2027 curve, tests at zero interest, dates the range to 6 Nov 2026).
Thu 19 Nov: 3f, a reflection line at most: normal rates are in the eye of the beholder, and a plan sized at zero interest needs none; Damodaran's averages are 2008's.

Thu 19 Nov: a fix, checked on the repo curve: 10-year 5.29% on 30 Sep, 4.94% on 30 Oct 2026, so 5.29% went with the 1 Oct premium (H6-080's 4.20% a month earlier); fix H6-005 (H7-017 is merged into it) and also H6-080 (its 9.70% becomes about 9.35%), which the card does not name; the 5 Nov reading (04a D7, D28) quoted 5.29% from the same page, so re-read before printing a date-rate pair.

Thu 19 Nov: Table 2's note at most; corrects H6-080; never set 9.35% (US shares, an internal rate for ever) against J.P. Morgan's 7.5% (world, compound, ten years) as like for like, and no median figure (CANON B15); the 3.417% step is NUMBERS 8v.
Thu 19 Nov: no promise rests on a forecast is H7-034; blog extract adds a quote only.
Thu 19 Nov: store; the case sets 2031, so short, late promises explain the date rather than choose it; staged commitment is card Q154 and H3-111.
Thu 19 Nov: cyclicality in debt design is one of H6-007's four lines; nothing new.
Thu 19 Nov: 2.3, colour that carries IPS l.3: the best-known case for insuring careers starts from a young artist no one will share risk with; pair with row 2 in one sentence, never more.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 and a 3c clause, aha: Shiller's floor-and-upside under income was never built, so the plan puts the same shape under her promises; never say the plan insures her career or is capital-protected (buy-and-hold, Perold and Sharpe); hedge only as the pitch's word (CANON A2); competes with Q150-001 and Q134-034 for 2.3's clause.
Thu 19 Nov: no precedent and Abramowicz are Q134-034 (and Q150-001's never built); the card offers the merge.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.3 or 3e: splits career risk into the downturn all writers share (what the portfolio leans against) and her own book-by-book luck (met by needing her career only once, the 2028 deposit); Q134 measures the deposit, this names the split.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3f's closing paragraph, aha: tenure as risk management answers the too-cautious objection with the closing line's own trade (certainty underneath buys daring on top); at most two sentences; tenure guarantees a person, the ten an institution's years.
Thu 19 Nov: the break of row 5 that teaches: paying in advance removes the monitoring a promise of future earnings needs; never no monitoring (Table 3 watches fund events and the 2028 deposit).
Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3f, colour beside row 5: an insurance man's certain fortune let Ives write music nobody yet wanted; Shiller's figures not re-checked; one clause at most and only with row 5.
Thu 19 Nov: store, 2.3 colour at most: in 1861 the downturn hit a writer twice, through readers and through a failed publisher; 2.3 already carries the Census -7.8% (card Q148).
Thu 19 Nov: a conceit hazard, store only: in Thoreau's house pencils were the steady money; never beside pencil and ink.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 as the true fact behind ink (one clause) or 3d's reserves, the card's best: Osaka's backed bill against the empty bill is Laura's rule to state only what is held (IPS l.15); never in tables or Laura's words; her Treasuries are held for her, not a claim to an identifiable thing (Q157-032), so never rice in her own warehouse.

Thu 19 Nov: with row 10 only: Osaka's bills claimed almost four times the rice in store, while what Laura states sits under what her Treasuries pay (the room under the top: the 0.5% margin plus the rounding down, WORDS).
Thu 19 Nov: store; a detail of row 10's story (a rule on the paper's form did nothing; what stood behind it did); no separate decision.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0 or 3d with row 10, aha: empty bills were made good only by a sovereign guarantee (1773), and Laura's ink is already the sovereign's own debt, so the one thing that could empty it is the IPS's second reason (l.17); some of it is held through iBond funds, so say Treasuries held for her, never her own bonds.
Thu 19 Nov: 3d's reserves: a court could make a lord pay but not make the rice exist, Osaka's form of a pledge is owed, Laura's floor owned; competes with row 10 for one clause.
Thu 19 Nov: store; abstract only (Nagao, Japanese text unread): an empty promise slips into next year, while the ten are matched to their Januaries.

Thu 19 Nov: 2.0, a possible pencil fact: Dojima's rice on the books priced and insured rice without delivering it, as VT's price sets the top without any of it promised; pencil has a job, never fraud; VT is owned but pencil (Q157).
Thu 19 Nov: a guard if Dojima is used: say authorised in 1730; Shiller's 1673 conflicts with JPX.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b, one sentence of evaluation: universities cut programmes rather than draw endowments (Hansmann via Shiller, unread), while every dollar of Laura's reserve has its January; beside H3-059 and Q7c-020, never call the reserve an endowment.
Thu 19 Nov: store; supports card Q77: her Treasuries are held for her, not given in trust, so the money stays hers if the residency stops.

Thu 19 Nov: 3a or 3d, one clause: charity flows to the news, money set aside goes where it was put (IPS l.11's or on anybody else's money); its break (one giver cannot pool, so she buys all ten) is the useful part; the case already sets the rule, so pedigree-plus.
Thu 19 Nov: a conceit guard: in fundraising black and white means pledged, which backs defining ink with owned at first use; adds nothing new to the conceit.
Thu 19 Nov: a face over statistics is Q129-037's measured version; co-sponsors are institutions, and 3d keeps Laura's words plain.
Thu 19 Nov: 1780 Massachusetts indexing again (H6-156); the payments are fixed in dollars by the case and TIPS are banned, so history only.
Thu 19 Nov: store; risks outside living memory go unhedged; US homes, not Taiwan building costs, so no claim about Taiwan.

Thu 19 Nov: 3b or 3e, one clause: no instrument Laura may hold pays when Taiwan building costs rise, so her flexibility is self-insurance paid for by promising less of the top (NUMBERS 8o's near one-for-one trade); rebar futures unchecked.

Thu 19 Nov: store; over decades building costs track prices, the facility's risk is a burst inside six years (Q10c-002); Shiller's labour story does not fit Taiwan's 2026 rise, about 70% materials (card Q131).
Thu 19 Nov: Summers on self-fulfilling runs adds a voice to SD-3, first money in a field of last money (Q150-019).
Thu 19 Nov: the survivorship case for world shares is H7-042; Redleaf's you get paid for eliminating risk is a trader's quote, store only.

Thu 19 Nov: the same 3.4% hurdle as Q124-023 and NUMBERS 8v, with one over CAPE as a harsher input; CAPE read on secondary sites; 8v ran 3.1% and 3.06%, not 2.46%, so say only one step lower below 3.417%; VT $29,594 is 6.6% of $450,000 (checked).
Thu 19 Nov: store only; two sites disagree (0.56% against 0.80%), never print a figure.
Thu 19 Nov: ownership as legal rights is Q157-032's point from UCC 8-503 comment 2; Shiller adds a voice only.
Thu 19 Nov: store only; a new legal form outside the case and the IPS.
